title_en: Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of protecting the copyright of authors in their literary, artistic and scientific works, and the rights related to copyright, encouraging the creation and dissemination of works conducive to the building of socialist spiritual and material civilization, and promoting the development and flourishing of socialist culture and science.

Article 2 Works of Chinese citizens, legal persons or unincorporated organizations shall enjoy copyright in accordance with this Law, whether they are published or not.
Works of foreigners or stateless persons shall enjoy copyright under an agreement concluded between the country to which the author belongs or in which the author has his habitual residence and China, or under an international treaty to which both countries are party, and such copyright shall be protected by this Law.
Works of foreigners or stateless persons first published in the territory of China shall enjoy copyright in accordance with this Law.
Works of authors of countries that have not concluded an agreement with China or that are not party to an international treaty with China, and works of stateless persons, first published in a member country of an international treaty to which China is party, or simultaneously published in a member country and a non-member country, shall be protected by this Law.

Article 4 Copyright owners and owners of rights related to copyright shall not, in exercising their rights, violate the Constitution or laws, or harm public interests. The State shall carry out supervision and administration over the publication and dissemination of works in accordance with law.
Article 6 The measures for the protection of copyright in works of folklore shall be separately prescribed by the State Council.

Article 7 The national copyright authority shall be responsible for the administration of copyright throughout the country; the local copyright authorities at or above the county level shall be responsible for the administration of copyright within their respective administrative regions.

Article 8 Copyright owners and owners of rights related to copyright may authorize a copyright collective management organization to exercise their copyright or rights related to copyright. A copyright collective management organization established in accordance with law shall be a non-profit legal person, and upon authorization, it may claim rights in its own name for copyright owners and owners of rights related to copyright, and may participate, as a party, in litigation, arbitration or mediation involving copyright or rights related to copyright.
A copyright collective management organization may collect royalties from users on the basis of authorization. The standard for collection of royalties shall be negotiated and determined by the copyright collective management organization and the representatives of users; if negotiation fails, an application for an adjudication may be made to the national copyright authority; if a party is dissatisfied with the adjudication, it may initiate a lawsuit with the People's Court; a party may also directly initiate a lawsuit with the People's Court.
A copyright collective management organization shall regularly publish to the public the overall information on the collection and distribution of royalties, the deduction and use of administrative fees, and the undistributed portion of royalties, and shall establish a rights information inquiry system for the inquiry of right owners and users. The national copyright authority shall supervise and administer copyright collective management organizations in accordance with law.
The method of establishment, rights and obligations, collection and distribution of royalties, and supervision and administration of copyright collective management organizations shall be separately prescribed by the State Council.

Article 9 A copyright owner shall include:
(1) an author; and
(2) any other natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization that enjoys copyright in accordance with this Law.

Article 11 Copyright shall belong to the author, except where otherwise provided in this Law.
The natural person who creates a work shall be the author.
Where a work is created under the sponsorship of a legal person or an unincorporated organization, representing the will of such legal person or unincorporated organization, and the legal person or unincorporated organization bears responsibility for the work, such legal person or unincorporated organization shall be deemed as the author.

Article 12 A natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization that has the author's name mentioned on a work shall be the author, and the corresponding rights shall exist in such work, unless there is proof to the contrary.
An author or other copyright owner may register the work with a registration institution accredited by the copyright administrative department of the State.
For rights related to copyright, the provisions of the preceding two paragraphs shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 13 Copyright in a work created by adaptation, translation, annotation, or arrangement of a pre-existing work shall be enjoyed by the person who adapts, translates, annotates, or arranges the work, but the exercise of such copyright shall not infringe the copyright in the original work.

Article 14 Copyright in a work created jointly by two or more persons shall be enjoyed jointly by the co-authors. A person who has not participated in the creation shall not become a co-author.
Copyright in a joint work shall be exercised by the co-authors through consensus; where consensus cannot be reached and there is no justified reason, neither party may prevent the other from exercising rights other than those of transfer, exclusive licensing to others, or pledge, provided that the proceeds derived therefrom shall be reasonably distributed among all co-authors.
Where a joint work may be used separately, each author shall be entitled to independent copyright in the part created by him or her, but the exercise of such copyright shall not infringe the copyright in the joint work as a whole.

Article 15 A work that is created by compiling a number of works, fragments of works, or data or other materials that do not constitute works, and which reflects originality in the selection or arrangement of its contents, shall be a compilation work. The copyright in such a compilation work shall be enjoyed by the compiler, but the exercise of such copyright shall not infringe the copyright in the pre-existing works.

Article 16 Where a work created by adaptation, translation, annotation, arrangement, or compilation of a pre-existing work is used for publication, performance, or production of sound recordings or video recordings, permission shall be obtained from both the copyright owner of the derivative work and the copyright owner of the original work, and remuneration shall be paid.

Article 17 The copyright in a cinematographic work or a television drama work within an audiovisual work shall be enjoyed by the producer, provided that the authors such as the screenwriter, director, cinematographer, lyricist, and composer shall enjoy the right of authorship and shall be entitled to receive remuneration in accordance with the contract concluded with the producer.
The ownership of copyright in an audiovisual work other than those provided in the preceding paragraph shall be agreed upon by the parties; in the absence of an agreement or if the agreement is unclear, the copyright shall be enjoyed by the producer, provided that the authors shall enjoy the right of authorship and the right to receive remuneration.
The authors of a work, such as a script or a musical work, which may be used separately from an audiovisual work, shall be entitled to exercise their copyright independently.

Article 18 A work created by a natural person in the course of performing the tasks assigned by a legal person or an unincorporated organization shall be a work made for hire. Unless otherwise provided in Paragraph 2 of this Article, the copyright in such a work shall be enjoyed by the author, provided that the legal person or unincorporated organization shall have a priority right to use the work within its business scope. Within two years after the completion of the work, the author shall not, without the consent of the entity, authorize a third party to use the work in the same manner as the entity uses it.
Where a work made for hire falls under any of the following circumstances, the author shall enjoy the right of authorship, and the other copyright rights shall be enjoyed by the legal person or unincorporated organization, which may reward the author:
(1) engineering design drawings, product design drawings, maps, schematic diagrams, computer software, and other works made for hire which are created mainly by using the material and technical conditions of the legal person or unincorporated organization and for which the legal person or unincorporated organization bears responsibility;
(2) works made for hire created by staff of newspapers, periodicals, news agencies, radio stations, or television stations; and
(3) works made for hire for which the copyright shall be enjoyed by the legal person or unincorporated organization as provided by laws or administrative regulations or as agreed in a contract.

Article 19 The ownership of copyright in a work created under commission shall be agreed upon by the client and the commissioned party in a contract. Where the contract is not clear or no contract is concluded, the copyright shall belong to the commissioned party.

Article 20 The transfer of ownership of the original copy of a work shall not change the ownership of the copyright in the work, except that the right of exhibition of the original copy of a work of fine art or a photographic work shall be enjoyed by the owner of such original copy.
Where an author transfers the ownership of the original copy of an unpublished work of fine art or photographic work to another person, the exhibition of such original copy by the transferee shall not constitute an infringement of the author's right of publication.

Article 21 Where copyright belongs to a natural person, after the death of the natural person, the rights provided in items (5) through (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law shall, within the term of protection provided in this Law, be transferred according to law.
Where copyright belongs to a legal person or an unincorporated organization, after the change or termination of such legal person or unincorporated organization, the rights provided in items (5) through (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law shall, within the term of protection provided in this Law, be enjoyed by the legal person or unincorporated organization that succeeds to its rights and obligations; in the absence of any such successor legal person or unincorporated organization, they shall be enjoyed by the State.
Article 22 The term of protection of the rights of authorship, alteration, and integrity of an author shall be unlimited.

Article 23 For a work of a natural person, the term of protection of the right of publication and the rights provided in items (5) through (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law shall be the life of the author and fifty years after his or her death, ending on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the death of the author. In the case of a joint work, the term shall end on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the death of the last surviving author.
For a work of a legal person or an unincorporated organization, or a work made for hire in which the copyright (except the right of authorship) is enjoyed by the legal person or unincorporated organization, the term of protection of the right of publication shall be fifty years, ending on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the completion of the work; the term of protection of the rights provided in items (5) through (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law shall be fifty years, ending on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the first publication of the work, provided that if the work has not been published within fifty years after its completion, this Law shall no longer protect it.
For an audiovisual work, the term of protection of the right of publication shall be fifty years, ending on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the completion of the work; the term of protection of the rights provided in items (5) through (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law shall be fifty years, ending on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the first publication of the work, provided that if the work has not been published within fifty years after its completion, this Law shall no longer protect it.

Article 25 For the purpose of compiling and publishing textbooks for compulsory education and national education planning, fragments of published works, or short written works, musical works, or single works of fine art, photographic works, or graphic works that have been published may be compiled into textbooks without the permission of the copyright owner, provided that remuneration shall be paid to the copyright owner in accordance with relevant provisions, the name of the author and the title of the work shall be indicated, and other rights enjoyed by the copyright owner under this Law shall not be infringed.
The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to limitations on rights related to copyright.
Article 28 Where a property right in copyright is pledged, the pledgor and the pledgee shall undergo the pledge registration in accordance with law.

Article 29 Where a license contract or a contract of assignment does not clearly license or assign a certain right, the other party may not exercise such right without the consent of the copyright owner.

Article 30 The standard for payment of remuneration for the use of works may be agreed upon by the parties, or the remuneration may be paid in accordance with the standard prescribed by the national copyright authority jointly with the relevant departments. Where the agreement between the parties is not clear, the remuneration shall be paid in accordance with the standard prescribed by the national copyright authority jointly with the relevant departments.

Article 31 A publisher, performer, sound recording or video recording producer, radio station, television station, or the like, who uses another person's work in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law, shall not infringe the author's right of authorship, right of revision, right of integrity, and right to receive remuneration.
Article 32 A book publisher shall enter into a publishing contract with the copyright owner and pay remuneration for the publication of a book.

Article 33 The exclusive right of a book publisher to publish a work delivered to it for publication by the copyright owner, as agreed in the contract, shall be protected by law. No other person shall publish the work.

Article 34 A copyright owner shall deliver the work within the time limit agreed in the contract. A book publisher shall publish the book in accordance with the quality and time limit agreed in the contract.
If a book publisher fails to publish the book within the time limit agreed in the contract, it shall bear civil liability in accordance with the provisions of Article 61 of this Law.
If a book publisher reprints or republishes a work, it shall notify the copyright owner and pay remuneration. If the book publisher refuses to reprint or republish the work after the book goes out of stock, the copyright owner shall be entitled to terminate the contract.

Article 35 Where a copyright owner submits a contribution to a newspaper or periodical publisher, and does not receive a notice from the newspaper deciding to publish it within fifteen days from the date of dispatch, or does not receive a notice from the periodical publisher deciding to publish it within thirty days from the date of dispatch, the copyright owner may submit the same work to another newspaper or periodical publisher, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.
After a work is published, other newspapers or periodicals may reprint it or publish it as an abstract or reference material, unless the copyright owner has declared that it shall not be reprinted or excerpted, provided that the copyright owner shall be paid remuneration in accordance with the provisions.

Article 36 A book publisher may modify or abridge a work with the permission of the author.
A newspaper or periodical publisher may make modifications or abridgements of a textual nature to a work. Any modification of the content shall be subject to the permission of the author.

Article 37 A publisher shall have the right to permit or prohibit others from using the typographical arrangement of the books or periodicals it publishes.
The term of protection for the right provided in the preceding paragraph shall be ten years, expiring on December 31 of the tenth year after the first publication of the book or periodical using that typographical arrangement.

Article 38 Where a performer performs the work of another person, the performer shall obtain permission from the copyright owner and pay remuneration. Where a performance organizer organizes a performance, the organizer shall obtain permission from the copyright owner and pay remuneration.

Article 40 Where a performer makes a performance for the purpose of completing the performance tasks of the performing entity, such performance shall be deemed a work-made-for-hire performance. The performer shall enjoy the right to claim being the performer and the right to protect the image of the performance from distortion, while the ownership of other rights shall be determined by agreement between the parties. Where the parties have no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the rights in the work-made-for-hire performance shall be enjoyed by the performing entity.
Where the rights in the work-made-for-hire performance are enjoyed by the performer, the performing entity may use the performance free of charge within its business scope.

Article 41 The term of protection for the rights provided in items (1) and (2) of the first paragraph of Article 39 of this Law shall not be limited.
The term of protection for the rights provided in items (3) to (6) of the first paragraph of Article 39 of this Law shall be fifty years, expiring on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the occurrence of the performance.

Article 42 A sound recording or visual recording producer that uses the work of another person to produce a sound recording or visual recording shall obtain permission from the copyright owner and pay remuneration.
A sound recording producer that uses a musical work that has been lawfully recorded as a sound recording by another person to produce a sound recording may do so without permission from the copyright owner, but shall pay remuneration in accordance with the provisions; where the copyright owner has declared that such use is not permitted, such use shall not be allowed.
Article 43 A sound recording or visual recording producer that produces a sound recording or visual recording shall conclude a contract with the performer and pay remuneration.

Article 44 A sound recording or visual recording producer shall enjoy the right to authorize others to reproduce, distribute, rent out, or communicate to the public via information networks the sound recording or visual recording it has produced and to obtain remuneration therefor. The term of protection for such right shall be fifty years, expiring on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the first completion of the production of such sound recording or visual recording.
A person who is authorized to reproduce, distribute, or communicate to the public via information networks a sound recording or visual recording shall also obtain permission from the copyright owner and the performer and pay remuneration. Where a person is authorized to rent out a sound recording or visual recording, such person shall also obtain permission from the performer and pay remuneration.

Article 45 Where a sound recording is used for public communication by wire or wireless means, or is publicly broadcast to the public through technical equipment that transmits sounds, the user shall pay remuneration to the sound recording producer.

Article 46 A radio station or television station that broadcasts an unpublished work of another person shall obtain permission from the copyright owner and pay remuneration.
A radio station or television station that broadcasts a published work of another person may do so without permission from the copyright owner, but shall pay remuneration in accordance with the provisions.

Article 47 A radio station or television station shall have the right to prohibit the following acts done without its permission:
(1) to rebroadcast its broadcasts of radio or television programs by wire or wireless means;
(2) to record or reproduce its broadcasts of radio or television programs; and
(3) to communicate its broadcasts of radio or television programs to the public via information networks.
A radio station or television station, when exercising the rights provided in the preceding paragraph, shall not affect, restrict, or infringe upon the exercise of copyright or copyright-related rights by others.
The term of protection for the rights provided in the first paragraph of this Article shall be fifty years, expiring on December 31 of the fiftieth year after the first broadcast of such radio or television program.

Article 48 A television station that broadcasts an audiovisual work or a visual recording of another person shall obtain permission from the copyright owner of the audiovisual work or the visual recording producer, and pay remuneration. Where a television station broadcasts a visual recording of another person, it shall also obtain permission from the copyright owner and pay remuneration.

Article 49 For the purpose of protecting copyright and rights related to copyright, right holders may take technological measures.
Without the permission of the right holder, no organization or individual may intentionally circumvent or destroy any technological measure, manufacture, import or provide to the public any device or component for the purpose of circumventing or destroying a technological measure, or intentionally provide technical services to others for circumventing or destroying a technological measure, except where laws or administrative regulations provide that circumvention is allowed.
For the purposes of this Law, “technological measures” means effective technologies, devices or components used to prevent or restrict, without the permission of the right holder, the browsing or appreciation of works, performances, sound recordings or video recordings, or the provision of works, performances, sound recordings or video recordings to the public through information networks.

Article 54 Where copyright or rights related to copyright are infringed, the infringer shall compensate for the actual losses suffered by the right holder or the illegal gains of the infringer; if it is difficult to calculate the actual losses of the right holder or the illegal gains of the infringer, compensation may be determined by reference to the royalties for the use of the right. Where the infringement of copyright or rights related to copyright is committed intentionally and the circumstances are serious, compensation may be granted in an amount of not less than one time but not more than five times the amount determined in accordance with the above methods.
If the actual losses of the right holder, the illegal gains of the infringer, or the royalties are difficult to calculate, the People's Court shall, in light of the circumstances of the infringement, award compensation of not less than 500 yuan but not more than 5,000,000 yuan.
The compensation amount shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement.
Where the right holder has fulfilled the necessary burden of adducing evidence, but the books, records, etc. related to the infringement are mainly in the possession of the infringer, the People's Court may, in order to determine the amount of compensation, order the infringer to provide the books, records, etc. related to the infringement; if the infringer fails to provide them, or provides false books, records, etc., the People's Court may determine the amount of compensation with reference to the claims and evidence provided by the right holder.
When hearing a copyright dispute case, the People's Court shall, at the request of the right holder, order the destruction of infringing copies, except in special circumstances; order the destruction, without compensation, of the materials, tools, equipment, etc. mainly used to make the infringing copies; or, in special circumstances, order that the aforementioned materials, tools, equipment, etc. be prohibited from entering commercial channels, without compensation.

Article 55 When the department in charge of copyright investigates and deals with acts suspected of infringing copyright or rights related to copyright, it may inquire of the relevant parties, investigate the circumstances related to the suspected illegal acts; conduct on-site inspection of the places and articles involved in the suspected illegal acts of the parties; consult and copy contracts, invoices, account books and other materials related to the suspected illegal acts; and may seal up or seize the places and articles involved in the suspected illegal acts.
When the department in charge of copyright exercises the functions and powers prescribed in the preceding paragraph according to law, the parties shall provide assistance and cooperation, and shall not refuse or obstruct.

Article 56 Where a copyright owner or an owner of rights related to copyright has evidence that another person is committing or is about to commit an act that infringes his or her rights or hinders the realization of his or her rights, and that if not stopped promptly, his or her legitimate rights and interests will suffer irreparable harm, he or she may, before prosecution, apply to the People's Court according to law for measures such as property preservation, an order to perform certain acts, or an order to prohibit certain acts.

Article 57 To stop an infringing act, where evidence may be destroyed or is likely to be difficult to obtain later, the copyright owner or the owner of rights related to copyright may, before prosecution, apply to the People's Court according to law for evidence preservation.

Article 58 When hearing a case, the People's Court may, for infringement of copyright or rights related to copyright, confiscate illegal gains, infringing copies, and property used for illegal activities.

Article 59 Where the publisher or producer of a reproduction cannot prove that its publication or production is legally authorized, or the distributor of a reproduction or the lessor of a reproduction of an audiovisual work, computer software, or sound or visual recording product cannot prove that the reproduction it distributes or leases has a legal source, it shall bear legal liability.
In litigation, where the alleged infringer claims that it shall not bear tort liability, it shall provide evidence proving that it has obtained the permission of the right owner, or that there exists a circumstance prescribed by this Law in which the work may be used without permission from the right owner.

Article 60 Copyright disputes may be mediated, or may be submitted to an arbitration institution for arbitration pursuant to a written arbitration agreement reached between the parties or an arbitration clause in the copyright contract.
Where the parties have neither a written arbitration agreement nor an arbitration clause in the copyright contract, they may directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court.

Article 61 Where a party bears civil liability for failing to perform contractual obligations or for performing contractual obligations not in conformity with the agreement, and where a party exercises litigation rights or applies for preservation, the provisions of relevant laws shall apply.
Article 62 The term "copyright" as used in this Law means copyright.
Article 63 The term "publication" as used in Article 2 of this Law means reproduction and distribution of a work.
Article 64 The measures for protection of computer software and the right of communication through information networks shall be separately prescribed by the State Council.

Article 65 For photographic works, where the term of protection for the right of publication and the rights provided in Items (5) to (17) of Paragraph 1 of Article 10 of this Law has expired before June 1, 2021, but the works are still within the term of protection pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 23 of this Law, they shall no longer be protected.

Article 66 The rights of copyright owners, publishers, performers, producers of sound or visual recordings, radio stations, and television stations provided for in this Law, which have not exceeded the term of protection provided for in this Law as of the date of coming into force of this Law, shall be protected in accordance with this Law.
For infringements or breaches of contract that occurred before the coming into force of this Law, the relevant provisions at the time of the infringement or breach shall apply.
Article 67 This Law shall come into force on June 1, 1991.
